messages.subject: Non-linear function of a GRF
parts:
Hi, 

Do you know if it is possible to fit a model with a non-linear function of a GRF as random effect using inla or inlabru?

Say for example, I have Y~Poisson(lambda(s))

And I want to model lambda as:

log(lambda(s)) = X'(s)*beta + w_1(s) + f(Z'(s)*gamma + w_2(s))

with f a non-linear function, and w_1(s) and w_2(s) two zero-mean GRFs?

Cheers,

Jorge

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Non-linear function of a GRF
parts:
Hi, with plain inla, no, with inlabru, yes (if the nonlinear function isn’t too nonlinear inlabru linearises the model at the posterior mode).

First define the two spatial covariate effects And random fields as model components, X, Z, w1, w2.
Then the model formula is a general R expression. Define your nonlinear function as
fun <- function(x) {…}
and then the formula becomes
Y ~ X + w1 + fun(Z + w2)

See the tutorials on inlabru.org for how to define the covariate and field components in inlabru.

In case you run into convergence issues due to the nonlinearity, there will soon be an updated version with a more robust method.

Finn
